authority.count_note: The retained merged authority heading is stale; the table contains TEST-P001..TEST-P108. TEST-G3 seals the actual table, including P105-P108.

promises.text: Every test starts from a verified process-state baseline and cannot poison later tests silently.
Production CLI in-process invocation no longer leaks transaction/validation repository-root environment state.
The autouse guard snapshots/restores all Devtool-owned environment keys rather than a permanently incomplete allowlist.
The state guard reports the exact leaking test and leaked keys/state before restoring them.
cwd and selected Devtool global overrides/caches are restored after each in-process CLI test.
Order-dependent validation cascades disappear; the remaining isolated failures are independently actionable.
The known stop→pause validation control regression remains visible as one real product failure until fixed.
Failure summaries distinguish likely cascade, generated-contract drift, stale/brittle test and independent product regression.
One generated-surface synchronization contract owns parser/help/completion/guide parity.
Higher-level seals consume generated-surface receipt/evidence instead of independently producing duplicate root failures.
Console diffs for giant generated files are bounded; complete diffs are attached.
Large state objects use concise assertion diagnostics with full structured evidence available separately.
A structured final test summary is available even if the raw pytest log is truncated.
Default developer test output uses concise tracebacks and useful skip/xfail/failure reasons.
Test lanes distinguish fast/contract, integration, external-tool, system/seal and full execution.
Normal editing feedback does not require running every historical final seal.
The current 2-second test budget becomes lane-aware and enforceable rather than purely advisory.
Setup, call and teardown durations are all measured.
Session startup and collection duration are recorded.
Per-file cumulative duration is recorded and budgetable.
Subprocess/tool/Git launch counts can be profiled for expensive tests.
Termux performance evidence is kept separately from desktop/CI profiles without changing correctness requirements.
The resolved Python test environment is qualified once and can execute multiple test shards without redundant dependency synchronization.
Skipping uv/environment sync is allowed only after explicit environment-readiness proof.
Test/development dependencies have an explicit reproducible declaration/lock contract.
`devtool pytest profile` or its successor streams output instead of buffering an entire failing suite in memory.
Test profiling consumes structured timing/result data instead of only parsing human text.
TestPerformanceProfile is a RUN V3 attachment/projection, not a new performance database.
Stable pytest markers are centrally declared and unknown markers fail.
Every expensive/external/stateful test is classifiable by resource/lane policy.
Parallel-safe and serial/stateful tests are distinguished before any xdist-style parallelism is enabled.
Termux worker count is adaptive and conservative rather than `-n auto`.
Historical campaign identifiers remain traceable after behavior-centric organization.
Tests are gradually organized by enduring behavior/domain rather than implementation chronology.
Large test modules are split only along stable behavior boundaries.
A shared GitRepoFactory/RepoFactory replaces repeated boilerplate where real Git is genuinely required.
Unit/contract tests mock repository-state boundaries rather than spawning Git unnecessarily.
Real Git remains covered in explicit integration/system tests.
ValidationSessionFactory and compact state assertions reduce duplication and giant repr failures.
Artifact fixture builders centralize safe overlay/bundle/snapshot construction for tests.
Mocks target stable boundary interfaces rather than incidental internal kwargs.
Public-contract and white-box tests are explicitly distinguishable.
Historical final seals verify historical contracts/evidence rather than blindly asserting every current generated byte.
Current global generated surfaces are qualified once by a current seal.
Roadmap/seal tests run in an explicit system/seal lane.
Canonical test identity is independent of a test file's historical campaign filename.
Pytest/JUnit results are ingested into canonical TestResult/TestRunReceipt models.
Canonical JUnit/test reports live in private RUN V3 storage.
Repo-local test reports are optional export/latest projections only.
Repeated runs cannot overwrite canonical historical JUnit evidence.
Failure clustering never deletes or hides the underlying raw failure list.
A likely cascade is annotated as secondary while its tests still have recorded outcomes.
External-tool tests declare exact tool requirements and environment identity.
External/system tests have explicit timeout budgets and retain subprocess evidence on timeout.
Heartbeat output can identify the active test/phase/process causing a long silent interval.
Test inventory can explain why a test belongs to a lane and which resources it needs.
Roadmap test jobs reference stable test/check identities instead of duplicating long path lists where possible.
File moves/renames do not invalidate roadmap semantics when the stable check identity is unchanged.
Pytest configuration is centrally declared with strict markers, testpaths and warning policy.
Collection/import performance is measured and has regression visibility.
Per-test HOME/XDG isolation remains the safe default until lighter unit isolation is proven.
Fixture sharing is introduced only after leak-detection invariants are green.
A shuffle/repeat diagnostic lane can reproduce order-dependent failures with recorded seeds.
Correctness tests are never silently retried into a passing final status.
Any quarantine has owner/reason/expiry and remains visible to release/roadmap policy.
Fast lane has a measured Termux-oriented target budget and fails when structural regressions blow it up materially.
Integration lane preserves real process/Git/PTY semantics without dominating every edit cycle.
External lane preserves real compiler/toolchain coverage with explicit tool/environment qualification.
System/seal lane remains the authoritative broad qualification lane.
Full lane remains available but is partitionable/shardable rather than one giant opaque process.
Test sharding preserves deterministic selection and complete result aggregation.
Serial tests cannot accidentally execute concurrently with incompatible global resources.
RER may reuse test evidence only when TestSpec/TestSelection/input/environment/output identity qualifies.
Historical pass alone never skips a test.
Roadmap gates consume RER/test evidence rather than re-running identical broad path lists by convention.
Test run receipts link exact environment, selection, results, timing and attachments.
COPY/diagnostics owns final failure-cluster presentation; Test System supplies structured facts.
EXO owns execution/process/attempt state for test runs.
RUN V3 owns durable test reports/logs/history.
CFG owns lane/budget/timeout policy and provenance.
Python Environment owns the pytest interpreter/environment qualification.
CLI owns test/profile/lane command syntax and completion.
No separate pytest-specific run store, reuse engine or execution scheduler is introduced.
Final seal proves trustworthy isolation, fast feedback, complete system qualification and reproducible performance evidence.
TEST consumes canonical EXO attempt/process state and never introduces a pytest-specific execution scheduler or competing attempt model.
TEST consumes RUN V3 journals, logs, JUnit/profile attachments and history; repo-local reports remain optional projections rather than canonical history.
TEST consumes RER evidence identity and freshness/invalidation decisions; historical pass evidence is reusable only through canonical RER qualification.
TEST consumes Python ENV interpreter/dependency/readiness receipts and never decides environment readiness from path existence or a successful import alone.
TEST consumes CFG-owned lane, marker, timeout, budget and quarantine policy with provenance instead of creating hidden pytest-only configuration authority.
TEST emits structured failure-cluster facts while PRES/COPY owns human, JSON, TUI and Desktop presentation and drill-down behavior.
TEST consumes DIST child-run/provider lineage for remote/sharded execution and keeps transport degradation distinct from test failure truth.
TEST exports stable check identities, receipts, performance evidence and closure proof to RMP; RMP decides roadmap/gate policy rather than pytest path lists.
Generated-surface drift is represented as one synchronization root with dependent seal failures linked to the root while every raw test result remains queryable.
ProcessStateGuard leak detection and restore are part of test trustworthiness and are validated before any fixture sharing, sharding or parallel execution is expanded.
Fast/integration/external/system/full lanes are semantic inventory selections, not duplicated pytest command strings with divergent behavior.
Stable TestSpec/TestCheck identity survives file moves and campaign-history reorganization while preserving historical aliases/provenance.
Shards and workers execute an immutable TestSelection; aggregation cannot silently drop a failed, timed-out, canceled or unavailable shard.
Performance comparison is profile-qualified by HostContext/Python environment/lane identity; incompatible Termux and desktop samples are not treated as equivalent baselines.
Timeout and heartbeat evidence identifies the active test/phase/process and terminates only the owned process tree through EXEC semantics.
Correctness retries never convert a failing final outcome into an ordinary pass; repeat/shuffle and quarantine remain explicit diagnostic/policy states.

TEST-X01, TEST-X02, TEST-X03 and TEST-X04 may run bounded targeted validation for changed non-Gradle boundaries; Gradle-related implementation validation is deferred. TEST-G1, TEST-G2 and TEST-G3 remain separate authoritative validations, and `--no-validate` remains valid when no meaningful non-Gradle targeted check exists.

Every TEST implementation overlay retains the before-commit editable-install refresh hook until deterministic candidate-runtime resolution supersedes it, so later hooks exercise the transaction candidate Devtool.
Before TEST-G3 every TEST-P001..TEST-P084 source promise and all 105 source regression contracts have explicit evidence/disposition in addition to the merged TEST ledger.

TEST-G3 proves the same selected test semantics through local/Termux and supported delegated execution paths, from inventory and environment qualification through EXO execution, RUN evidence, RER consumption and RMP gate proof without a competing truth store.
Canonical TestResult/test-run evidence permits the runner/process to fail while `failed_count == 0` when no concrete testcase failure occurred.
Executed/failed/errored/skipped counts and failed IDs are derived from trustworthy testcase identity/events, never synthesized solely from runner/process exit failure.
Failed-test retry operates only on concrete failed testcase IDs; setup/process/device/protocol failures use their typed execution-failure retry policy instead.
Cross-runner adapters for pytest, Go, Gradle/JUnit, .NET and Android preserve the invariant that command/runner failure is not automatically a testcase failure.

regressions.text: One in-process CLI test setting DEVTOOL_VALIDATION_STATE_REPO_ROOT cannot affect the next test.
One in-process CLI test setting DEVTOOL_TRANSACTION_REPO_ROOT cannot affect the next test.
One in-process CLI test setting DEVTOOL_TRANSACTION_PRIMARY_REPO_ROOT cannot affect the next test.
Process-state guard reports leaked DEVTOOL_* keys before restoring them.
Process-state guard restores cwd after a test changes it.
Process-state guard restores Devtool logstore override.
Process-state guard catches a newly introduced DEVTOOL_* variable without editing an allowlist.
Focused validation session tests produce the same result before and after unrelated CLI tests.
Validation tests pass/fail identically under two deterministic test orders.
Shuffle diagnostic records seed/order on failure.
Stop→pause conflict returns stable control-unavailable exit after cascade fixes.
Dry-run validation does not create/advance durable validation state.
Failure clustering identifies same-session/state-root cascades without hiding raw failures.
Generated completion mismatch produces one root synchronization finding.
Final seals can reference that generated-surface finding instead of duplicating huge diffs.
`--preserve-dirty` appears in generated completion when parser exposes it.
Packaged/runtime zsh completion normalization handles intentional terminal newline policy.
Complete feature guide covers every public canonical command.
Complete feature guide covers public root options.
Generated guide mismatch console output is bounded.
Full generated guide diff is saved as an attachment.
ValidationSession assertion failure prints selected mismatched fields, not multi-thousand-character repr by default.
Full structured ValidationSession evidence remains available.
Raw pytest log truncation cannot remove the machine-readable final failure summary.
Default lane uses concise traceback mode.
Fast lane excludes system/final-seal tests.
Fast lane excludes real external compilers unless explicitly opted in.
Integration lane includes representative real Git behavior.
External lane includes real Go/javac/Gradle tests according to tool availability.
System/seal lane includes roadmap/federation final-seal tests.
Full lane is the union of intended lanes.
Unknown pytest marker fails collection.
Slow test marker is statically declared.
External tool requirement marker is statically declared.
Serial/stateful marker is statically declared.
Parallel-safe tests can run in two workers without result differences.
Serial tests never run concurrently in the same incompatible resource pool.
Adaptive Termux worker policy uses memory/CPU limits.
Strict slow budget catches FRX-X04-style unmarked 3–5s tests.
Slow budget includes setup duration.
Slow budget includes teardown duration.
Per-file cumulative budget detects many individually sub-threshold tests.
Session report records startup/pre-pytest-launch duration.
Session report records pytest collection duration.
Session report records peak RSS when available.
Profile records subprocess count per test/file where instrumentation is enabled.
Profile records Git subprocess count for Git-heavy suites.
Profile records external tool identities.
Profile output is streamed, not held entirely in memory.
Profile can complete when raw output exceeds normal terminal log cap.
Test dependencies can be restored from an explicit declared test environment.
Qualified test environment can rerun pytest without dependency sync.
Unqualified/fresh uv environment does not blindly use --no-sync.
Direct qualified interpreter and uv-managed invocation agree on test collection/result identity.
Collection performance regression is visible in TestPerformanceProfile.
RepoFactory creates isolated repository roots with deterministic Git identity.
GitRepoFactory can create commits/branches/worktrees without per-test boilerplate.
Unit tests can use fake repository state without spawning Git.
Integration tests still exercise actual Git commands.
ValidationSessionFactory creates unique repository/session roots.
Artifact fixture builder creates deterministic overlay/bundle/snapshot inputs.
Mock boundary accepts new internal optional kwargs without unrelated failure.
Tests specifically about boundary signatures still fail on incompatible signature changes.
Historical seal fixture remains stable when unrelated current completion text changes.
Current generated-surface seal fails when current completion is stale.
Canonical JUnit report uses run-scoped storage.
Two runs do not overwrite each other's JUnit evidence.
Repo-local `.devtool/reports/pytest.xml` is optional projection, not canonical history.
TestRunReceipt lists selected node IDs and lane.
TestRunReceipt lists passed/failed/skipped/xfail counts.
TestRunReceipt links failure attachments.
TestRunReceipt links environment identity.
TestPerformanceProfile links to the same run.
Likely cascade annotations reference the suspected root failure/state leak.
Cluster classification never changes pytest exit status by itself.
Timeout kills/cancels owned child process tree and stores diagnostics.
Heartbeat names active pytest node and phase.
Heartbeat names active external child process/tool when available.
Roadmap gate references stable check IDs rather than only test file paths.
Renaming a test file with same stable check identity does not invalidate roadmap meaning.
A TestInventory item resolves to the same stable check identity through CLI, wrapper, roadmap and direct pytest entry points.
A moved/renamed test file keeps its stable check identity and historical result lineage while its current node ID updates.
A fast-lane selection compiled from CFG policy is immutable once EXO execution begins and is recorded in TestRunReceipt.
A Python ENV readiness receipt can be reused across qualified shards without rerunning dependency synchronization, and stale readiness fails closed.
A local test run and an equivalent DIST-delegated child run produce the same canonical TestResult/TestRunReceipt schema and stable check identities.
SSH/chroot/PRoot/OCI transport degradation is recorded separately from a known child test failure and cannot replace the primary failure.
RUN V3 stores JUnit, raw logs and TestPerformanceProfile under run-scoped attachments; repeated runs cannot overwrite historical evidence.
Repo-local `.devtool/reports` output can be removed without losing canonical historical test evidence already committed to RUN V3.
RER reuses a test only when TestSpec, TestSelection, input, environment and required output identities qualify; an unrelated historical pass is insufficient.
A reused test is projected as REUSED with source-run provenance and does not emit fabricated live test/process events.
One generated-surface synchronization failure is linked as the root cause for dependent seal failures without deleting each dependent raw outcome.
PRES/CLI/TUI/Desktop render identical counts, primary failures, cascade annotations and reused/quarantined states from the same structured TEST/RUN facts.
A bounded failure summary remains useful when the raw pytest log or giant diff attachment is much larger than the console budget.
A deterministic shard plan covers the full immutable selection exactly once across shards and aggregation detects missing/duplicate shard coverage.
Serial-resource tests cannot overlap incompatible workers while independent parallel-safe tests can execute concurrently under HostContext limits.
Termux and desktop performance baselines with different HostContext/profile identities are retained separately and cannot cross-trigger invalid regressions.
A timeout records active test phase, owned child processes, termination outcome and preserved partial stdout/stderr before final TestResult classification.
A shuffle/repeat diagnostic run records seed/repetition and preserves the original failing attempt instead of retrying it into a normal pass.
RMP gate consumption references stable check IDs and TestRunReceipt/RER evidence rather than re-expanding duplicated historical file lists.
Final TEST closure can trace every source TEST promise/regression and every merged TEST promise to evidence, export, supersession or evidence-backed retirement with no UNMAPPED entry.
